items.prompt: Quote has unique_ptr<Impl> and only a forward declaration of Impl in quote.h. A client compiles destruction of a local Quote using only that header. Which organization supports the intended boundary?

options.text: Define ~Quote() inline as =default in the header and leave Impl incomplete everywhere.
options.why: Default deletion of Impl needs its definition at the relevant destructor instantiation; merely defaulting inline does not supply that definition.

options.text: Replace unique_ptr with a raw pointer and omit destruction.
options.why: That avoids default deletion by leaking the owned implementation, breaking the ownership contract.

options.text: Include the complete Impl class in every client so the destructor can be inline.
options.why: This can make deletion compile but defeats the specified opaque implementation/recompilation boundary.

options.text: Declare ~Quote() in quote.h and default it after complete Impl in quote.cpp.
options.why: The public destructor call can be compiled against a declaration, while default deletion is instantiated beside the complete implementation.

items.explanation: The public destructor call can be compiled against a declaration, while default deletion is instantiated beside the complete implementation.
